purpose: Publish the three existing approved reference images for consumer-local inspection before Fuel/Wanted implementation. These files are usable from this feature branch without merging it.

files.source: Existing corrected design mock; published byte-for-byte without image modification.
files.use: Compact desktop text, bold green cash and background-free driving HUD hierarchy. Conceptual design board only.

files.source: Existing corrected design mock; published byte-for-byte without image modification.
files.use: Compact warning hierarchy and wanted placement. Conceptual design board only.

files.source: Original police-symbol image supplied by Craig for wanted markers; published byte-for-byte without image modification.
files.use: Canonical symbol silhouette, circular center and pointed-ray proportions. This original overrides all generated emblem variants.
files.licensing: User-supplied reference. No licensing or official-asset claim is made.

verification.source_bytes: All three files decode as PNG. SHA256 and Git blob SHA1 calculated from actual bytes. Both board SHA256 values match canonical td-208 at the pinned task commit.
verification.source_pixels: All three source images opened at original resolution before publication.
verification.consumer_gate: Consumer must fetch this exact feature-branch commit, verify each SHA256, decode the files and open actual full-resolution pixels locally before image-dependent work. Publication alone does not prove consumer transfer or pixel inspection.
verification.acceptance: Reference publication only. No implementation, runtime acceptance or independent acceptance verdict is claimed.

design_limitations: The boards reconstruct scenery and Japanese lettering; they are reference-grounded concepts, not literal unchanged screenshot composites. Do not use generated lettering or street viewpoints as game assets.
Minimap topology is illustrative. Map, gig, health, controls and scene-assembly ownership remain outside td-208.
Generated hero-size emblem rays differ from the original. Never trace the board's emblem geometry; use the original supplied symbol as the canonical reference.
Collage viewport proportions, text sizes and touch targets are not measured runtime acceptance evidence. Required real native/browser viewport, interaction and state matrices remain mandatory.
The quiet and warning boards provide the compact desktop type-scale direction. Values, warning states and depicted transactions are illustrative rather than runtime proof.
Existing minimap/GAS, DamageBar, natural chassis-wreck and physical-phone gates remain independent. This publication does not clear any implementation or acceptance gate.
